output.title: Credential rotation is a workflow cost, not just a security topic
output.body:
If you run a small business, the cost of credential rotation usually shows up in a very ordinary place: someone has to re-enter an API key, SaaS password, or admin token, and a workflow pauses until it is fixed. That can mean a failed integration, a stalled report, or a login that no longer works. Those are not Bareni results or customer claims; they are the kinds of breakpoints an owner can look for in their own tools.

The question is not whether AI should “do” credential rotation. In most cases, this is a systems and access-management problem first. AI can sit around the edges of the workflow, for example in alerting or in documenting what changed, but the core decision is still how credentials are stored, updated, and checked. If the process is loose, a clever tool mostly makes the mess faster.

A practical next step is to audit the recurring credentials you manage today: API keys, shared logins, admin access, and anything tied to a SaaS integration. Then count how many times in a month someone has to re-enter or update one. Pick one recent failure and note how long it took to notice and fix it. That gives you a real baseline for comparing manual work, a tooling change, or simply keeping the process as-is. Once you know that cost, the decision gets less vague.
